newsitem.title: USA: Agencies, data said to lift U.S. mortgage-backeds.
newsitem.headline: Agencies, data said to lift U.S. mortgage-backeds.

text.p: Agency buying and benign economic data lent U.S. mortgage-backed securities a slight bounce on Monday, traders said.
"The agencies have been in," one trader said, "but it's been very quiet other than that."
Mortgages generally were 1/32 to 4/32 higher, closely matching corresponding gains in Treasuries.
Analysts partially credited a 1.5-percent drop in existing home sales in October, reported by the National Association of Realtors on Monday morning, with driving Treasuries' gains.
Not all of the news was positive, as one trader said she had heard "rumors a of a large seller" in the morning.
Mortgage yield spreads over Treasuries held steady to slightly tighter much of the day before widening a touch in the afternoon. "We widened out a little," one trader said. By
late on Monday, Ginnie Mae 7.0 percent coupons were up 4/32 at 99-05/32, yielding 104 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 2/32 at 100-28/32, while comparable Freddie Mac securities were 3/32 higher at 99-05/32.
